title: topology-aware-egress-strategies-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad collects topology-aware egress options and lightweight simulation ideas for multi-region traffic steering. Goal is to pick a small set of deployable primitives that give predictable latency and cost behavior while keeping rollback simple.

Context / constraints:
- Global footprint: three primary regions (us-west, eu-central, ap-south).
- Must support both hosted API and Dedicated endpoints with region affinity.
- Rolling failover without long-lived session loss is preferred; sticky sessions are limited to 10s for most APIs.
- Observability hooks already exist for per-e2e latency and per-edge error rates (prometheus + trace ids).
- Control plane can push per-region weight maps and short TTL DNS records, but we want to avoid frequent global DNS churn.

Design desiderata (ranked):
1) Deterministic latency SLOs for 95th pct requests (primary objective).
2) Fast, safe fallback on region outage (secondary objective).
3) Minimal cache invalidation and minimal end-user visible failure modes.
4) Operability: simple knobs, clear rollback.

Approach sketch: topology-aware egress primitives
A) Hybrid Anycast + Regional Preference (controller-driven)
- Control plane advertises anycast address for edge POPs. Default routing via network shortest-path.
- Each client request carries geo metadata (edge POP id). For sessions that must prefer a region, control plane instructs edge to steer to an origin region using local routing tables.
- On region failure, edge changes next-hop to fallback region.
Pros: fast failover (BGP route changes) and single IP for clients.
Cons: harder to enforce strict regional isolation; observability per-client-to-origin gets trickier.

B) Active GeoDNS with weighted region lists + health thresholds
- DNS returns region-specific VIPs ordered by weight; client-side resolver selects first answer. TTLs are short (30s) during incidents, longer (300s) normally.
- Control plane recalculates weights based on e2e latency and capacity headroom.
- Health threshold: if region error-rate > X or latency > Y, decrease weight by 90% and gradually restore.
Pros: compatible with client-side load balancers, explicit region selection.
Cons: DNS TTL causes slow convergence; some clients ignore TTLs or cache aggressively.

C) Proxy-assisted steering (edge-level connection proxy)
- Edge accepts connection, then proxy decides origin based on planner policy and actively opens/rewrites upstream connection.
- Allows per-connection affinity and retries without exposing DNS.
Pros: precise control and can maintain connections while executing seamless upstream failover.
Cons: heavier edge CPU/memory; more operational complexity.

Control plane mechanics (shared ideas)
- Policy model: policy = {region_preference: list, max_latency_ms, failover_sequence, cost_budget_per_token}. All policies tied to a route/model combo.
- Short-lived experiments: attach weight overrides for N minutes (canary).
- Safety guard: server-side invariant checker rejects policies that route >75% traffic to region where available GPU capacity < 25% baseline.

Health detection and failure semantics
- Three parallel detectors: infra-level (BGP / cloud-provider region health), application-level (4xx/5xx spikes), and latency-shift detector (sudden 95th increase).
- Circuit state machine at control plane per-region: healthy -> degraded -> partial -> unhealthy. Transitions use hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.
- Failure action matrix: degraded => reduce weight by 50% and enable caching TTLs; partial => route new requests away but let in-flight complete; unhealthy => blackhole region for new requests and trigger emergency capacity request.

Session affinity and KV cache implications
- KV/prefix caches: prefer local-region cache for hits; on failover allow best-effort read-from-fallback region with TTL extension. Consider async background fill to repopulate local cache post-failover.
- Long-lived sessions: move to sticky-proxy mode for duration of operation, but impose upper bound on stickiness (e.g., 30s) to make failovers tolerable.

Simulation and experiment plan (quick wins)
- Build synthetic traffic generator that mimics 3 types: short-chat (low tokens, latency-sensitive), batch-embed (high tokens, cost-sensitive), streaming-chat (medium tokens, continuous connection).
- Run 100k-request simulation with mix: 60% short-chat, 30% batch-embed, 10% streaming. Inject region drop at t=30s and measure 95/99 latency and dropped-connection ratio.
- Compare three steering strategies (A,B,C) with metrics: median/95/99 latency delta, percent requests requiring reconnect, additional cost per 1M tokens, time-to-recover.
- Implement simulation as a k6 script + local controller model to emulate control-plane decisions. Ticket: JIRA PLAT-4872 (linked).

Operational runbook sketch
- Alerting: if any region 5xx > 0.5% for 3m AND 95th latency > 2x baseline -> paging.
- Automated mitigation: policy engine marks region ->partial and shifts 60% traffic away. Notify on-call with suggested rollback command (CLI: platctl steering rollback --route <route> --to-prior).
- Manual steps for oncall: verify provider console, check inter-region network errors, run simulation locally to validate plan before full DR action.

Open questions / risk items
- Anycast + TLS termination: can we maintain cert pinning and per-customer TLS choices at edges without region leakage? (security team input needed)
- Consistency cost: how often will cache population cross-region hit budgets? Need cost model for read-through vs refill.
- DNS relay behavior in certain mobile carriers (some carriers ignore short TTLs) — how to handle clients that never re-resolve?
- Legal/regulatory: some customers require firm region residency. How to prove with anycast that traffic never left region? Probably must provide VPC/private mode with no anycast in those cases.

Short-term action items (next 2 weeks)
- Aisha: spin up baseline k6 traffic generator and repo scaffold. (PLAT-4872)
- Marco: prototype control-plane weight calculator using recent telemetry and create canary mode.
- Evelyn: list customers with strict residency requirements and map to routes (for policy exceptions).
- Samir: quick cost model draft for cross-region egress and cache refill.

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments reproducible and commit synthetic traces to repo.
- Document rollback CLI commands prominently in runbook.
- Align with SRE on tracing tags to correlate client edge -> origin region more easily.

References / reading:
- internal: PLAT routing overview confluence (linked above)
- external: Cloud provider docs on BGP anycast best practices; DNS TTL caveats for mobile carriers.

---
End of scratchpad. This should be lightweight and intentionally pragmatic — aim to run simulations first, then pick the minimal strategy that satisfies our SLOs and compliance requirements.
